extracted.intended_audience: U.S. policymakers, federal agencies, university and research leaders, and funders concerned with national science policy and postwar research funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for establishing national science policy, federal support for basic research, development of scientific talent, coordination of wartime research release, and structures to support military and civilian research after World War II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government support for basic research in colleges, universities, and research institutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government should extend financial support to basic medical research in the medical schools and in the universities through grants both for research and for fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: traditional private sources are diminishing while research costs rise; colleges, universities, and research institutes are principal centers of basic research and provide environments for unconstrained inquiry. Amount guidance: initial effective spending not to exceed $5 million in the first year; after a program is underway perhaps $20 million a year can be spent effectively. Emphasizes preserving institutional internal control and freedom of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a new agency devoted to supporting basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that a new agency for these purposes be established to supplement support of basic research in colleges, universities, and research institutes, to support research on new weapons for both Services, and to administer a program of science scholarships and fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency characteristics: composed of persons of broad interest and experience who understand scientific research and education; stability of funds to permit long-range programs; recognize and preserve freedom of inquiry; leave internal control of policy, personnel, and research scope to the institutions; fully responsible to the President and through him to Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve freedom of inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom of inquiry must be preserved under any plan for Government support of science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The colleges, universities, and research institutes are the centers of basic research; scientists must be free to pursue truth wherever it leads. Government support should remove rigid wartime controls and recover freedom and healthy competitive scientific spirit. Implementation should follow the 'Five Fundamentals' (referenced on page 35).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop scientific talent via scholarships and fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government should provide a reasonable number of undergraduate scholarships and graduate fellowships in order to develop scientific talent in American youth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should attract into science only that proportion of youthful talent appropriate to national needs. Training is long and costly; many talented individuals lack means for higher education. Also include programs to train those now in uniform—Armed Services should identify and arrange continuing scientific education for service members where militarily possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate and support development and rapid deployment of therapeutic agents and special problem attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Government initiative, support, and coordination can be very effective in developing newly discovered therapeutic materials and methods and reducing time to make them available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government coordinated wartime examples (penicillin, anti-malarials) show that the Government can lead from early lab stages through scale-up and production without dictating how cooperating institutions conduct internal work. Encourages teamwork among medical schools, universities, Government, and industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective declassification and coordinated release of wartime scientific information
rubrics_metrics.description: Much wartime scientific information should be made public as soon as it is safe; a Board composed of Army, Navy, and civilian scientific members should promptly be established to select what may be released and to coordinate its publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some information must remain secret, but most should be released when there is reasonable belief the enemy cannot exploit it. Board should encourage publication and coordinate releases for maximum public and educational benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent civilian-controlled organization to support military research in peacetime
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be permanent civilian activity to supplement the research work of the Services in other scientific fields so as to carry on in time of peace some part of the wartime Office of Scientific Research and Development's activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an organization should be civilian-controlled, have close liaison with Army and Navy, funds direct from Congress, and clear power to initiate military research to supplement Service-conducted research—because much military research must be secret, has no commercial value, and is expensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen centers of basic research, especially weaker institutions and regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen the centers of basic research—colleges, universities, and research institutes—so they can meet increasing demands from industry and government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build up weaker institutions and particularly expand research capacity in regions lacking strong medical research activity to correct uneven development and avoid concentration of important work in a few large schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide incentives to industry to conduct research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government should provide suitable incentives to industry to conduct research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two suggested measures: (a) clarify Internal Revenue Code uncertainties regarding the deductibility of research and development expenditures as current charges against net income; (b) strengthen the patent system to eliminate uncertainties that burden small industries and prevent abuses. Also seek ways to cause benefits of basic research to reach industries that do not currently utilize new scientific knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a permanent Science Advisory Board to coordinate government scientific activities
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide coordination of common scientific activities of governmental agencies as to policies and budgets, a permanent Science Advisory Board should be created to advise the executive and legislative branches on these matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Board would improve coordination across agencies and help in budgeting and policy formulation to improve the quality and effectiveness of Government science efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify government recruiting, classification, and compensation for scientific personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps should be taken to modify procedures for recruiting, classifying, and compensating scientific personnel in Government to reduce the handicap of governmental scientific bureaus in competing with industry and the universities for top-grade scientific talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improved personnel policies are needed so Government laboratories can attract and retain high-caliber scientists, thereby improving the quality of scientific research within Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government responsibility to promote flow of new scientific knowledge and talent development
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government should accept new responsibilities for promoting the flow of new scientific knowledge and the development of scientific talent in American youth, since these vitally affect health, jobs, and national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is analogous to longstanding government support for agricultural research; the time has come to extend such support to other scientific fields. Effective discharge of these responsibilities requires an over-all agency with funds from Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support broad and basic studies across many scientific fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress requires that the entire front of medicine and underlying sciences (chemistry, physics, anatomy, biochemistry, physiology, pharmacology, bacteriology, pathology, parasitology, etc.) be broadly developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discoveries pertinent to medical and other advances often come from remote and unexpected sources; therefore support should not be narrowly confined but permit broad exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary role of medical schools and teaching hospitals in medical research and clinical investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary place for medical research is in the medical schools and universities; medical schools have unique capacity to integrate clinical investigations with preclinical science via close relationships with teaching hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical schools' primary obligation beyond teaching is to provide opportunity for free, untrammeled study; this duty cannot be shifted to government agencies or industry. Teaching hospitals are especially well qualified because of staff and supervision connections with medical schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain vigorous applied research in government and industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Applied research in Government and industry must be vigorous for science to serve as a powerful factor in national welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government's most important ways to promote industrial research are increasing the flow of new knowledge via support of basic research and aiding development of scientific talent; coordination and policy actions should encourage applied research activity.
